b3.kind: B3 — closing-safety mechanisms (zero paid upstream calls; synthetic state-machine fixtures)

mechanisms.audioWindowMerge: AudioWindowMerger.merge() — re-joins split windows at their ORIGINAL timeline offsets (idempotent, order-independent, mixed-rate loud-fail); AudioWindowMerger.concatenate() kept as the negative control its test proves different
mechanisms.versionedVoiding: VersionedToolCallGate — a call carries the turnVersion it was generated for; a version mismatch voids it on arrival, on setVersion, and again at finalize
mechanisms.actionCommitGate: VersionedToolCallGate.finalize() — side effects are released ONLY at finalize, ONLY for the current version; staging is free, applying is what the gate guards
mechanisms.sink: DryRunToolSink writes deliveredToRealSession:false itself and has no transport — the no-side-effect claim is mechanical, not verbal

recovery.definition: recovered = the CORRECTED call (seconds=20) reached the sink AND the SUPERSEDED call (seconds=30) did not
recovery.outOfScopeNote: correctionInsideGrace=false models a correction that arrives after the grace window expired and the proposal already committed. No commit gate can un-release an applied side effect; the corrected call still commits, but recovery is structurally false. This is the residual cost a finite grace window cannot remove — not a gate failure.
recovery.naiveControlNote: a naive apply-on-arrival gate releases the superseded call immediately and scores 0 across the board — the negative control that shows the versioned gate is doing the work.
